result.task: M1 — Meshtastic in node111, commit 99f5e0a (meshmud + presence children, consented identify, Nearby, meshtastic-http shim)

majors.title: Forget during an in-flight identify leaves a hidden, bound, un-unbindable board
majors.where: bootstrap/crates/node111/src/daemon/devices/registry.rs record_identify (store write + flush precede the `published` lookup) and src/daemon/meshtastic/identify.rs:237-256 (service installed before record_identify; its Err is mapped to 404 with no teardown)
majors.why: Sequence: POST /devices/{id}/identify (probe runs 5-100 s) -> DELETE /devices/{id} (forget: published.remove, entry.forgotten=true, entry.meshtastic=None, flush) -> probe succeeds -> identify() transfers claims to `meshmud`, spawns the reader, sets self.service, install_supervised(), then record_identify(): contains_key passes (forgotten entries stay in the store), it writes firmware + binding onto the forgotten entry and flushes, THEN fails on the `published` lookup -> identify returns 404. Next reconcile: desired = store.meshtastic_binding() (no `forgotten` check) == current -> service keeps running; registry tick skips the entry (`if forgotten { continue }`) so the device is hidden: DELETE -> 404, identify -> 404. The binding is persisted, so it survives daemon restarts; the only way out is unplugging the board for FORGET_CLEAR_TICKS. The user's explicit forget is overridden with no API path back.
majors.fix: In record_identify, resolve the `published` record (and require !entry.forgotten) before touching the store; in identify(), on Err from record_identify call stop_service() (or let the next reconcile stop it, now that no binding is persisted).

minors.title: Test flake: stub.accepted() read before the stub's accept thread counted the connect (confirmed 10/36 under load, all at the same line)
minors.why: TcpStream::connect returns on the kernel handshake; Stub::start bumps `accepted` only when its listener thread reaches that connection in `l.incoming()`. Under CPU load the thread lags and the assert sees 2. Every other accepted() check is behind a wait_until or is a no-new-connection (negative) assert, which is why only 1680 fires. Not a product race.
minors.fix: Replace the assert with `wait_until("fresh connection a", 5s, || stub.accepted() == 3)` (and the same for any future positive accepted() checks).

minors.title: An in-flight identify blocks daemon shutdown for up to downlink_wait + identify_timeout (~105 s)
minors.where: src/daemon/meshtastic/mod.rs:834-836 stop_and_wait awaits `transition`; identify.rs:172 holds it for the whole probe
minors.why: stop_and_wait sets `stopping` then waits on the lock; probe()/run_once() never look at `stopping`, so a SIGTERM during an identify waits for the reader's --once (up to 90 s) before children are joined; systemd's stop timeout then SIGKILLs the daemon with meshmud still holding the port.
minors.fix: Make probe() select on a shutdown Notify (or poll `stopping` in its 50 ms loops) and abort() the step; stop_and_wait can also try_lock and stop the identify child directly.

minors.title: A bound board whose meshmud binary is absent at start is never started when the binary appears
minors.where: src/daemon/meshtastic/mod.rs:572-581 reconcile retry branch (`retry` only when port_held_by.is_some())
minors.why: start_service records Service{meshmud: None, port_held_by: None} when !installed or !runnable; reconcile's `same` branch only retries the port-busy case, so after an upgrade installs current/bin/meshmud the service stays Absent until the daemon restarts or the binding changes. Not unsafe, but a silent 'ERROR until reboot'.
minors.fix: Retry also when `s.meshmud.is_none() && s.port_held_by.is_none() && runnable && meshmud_installed()`.

minors.title: A zero-length FromRadio frame is served as 'nothing queued', ending the client's poll loop early
minors.where: src/daemon/meshtastic/shim.rs:106-110 (Deframer accepts len 0) and :395 (empty body == none)
minors.why: The shim's contract is 'empty answer = queue empty, stop polling'; a 0-byte payload (a legal, all-default FromRadio encoding) in the queue is indistinguishable from that, so frames behind it wait for the client's next poll interval. Benign but contradicts 'one frame per call, poll until empty'.
minors.fix: Skip zero-length payloads in read_loop (do not enqueue them).

minors.title: max_sessions is a soft cap under concurrent first calls
minors.why: Two first calls on distinct keys both pass the `len() >= max_sessions` check before either inserts, so the cap can be exceeded by the number of concurrent openers (each a real meshmud TCP downlink). Bounded by the listener's concurrency, so not unbounded growth, but the documented cap is not strict.
minors.fix: Reserve the key under the map lock before connecting (insert a placeholder/closed-false sentinel, remove it on connect failure) so the count is checked and taken atomically.

minors.title: identify_target recovers the port holder by parsing the human-readable `reason` string
minors.where: src/daemon/devices/registry.rs identify_target: `rec.reason.strip_prefix("Its port is in use by ")`
minors.why: Brittle coupling to display copy; a wording change (U1 copy edits) silently turns the 409 detail into 'another program'. Correctness of the 409 itself is unaffected because claim_for re-checks the PortTable.
minors.fix: Put the holder task in `detail.port_held_by` in apply_meshtastic and read that.

minors.title: openapi identify text promises 'USB or Wi-Fi board' but no bind-by-address path exists (builder's recorded deviation)
minors.where: interface/api/openapi.yaml identifyDevice description; registry never detects Wi-Fi boards so identify has no TCP target for them
minors.why: Honest-copy rule: the contract text describes a flow the daemon cannot perform until an address-binding route or agent step exists (L6).
minors.fix: Amend the description to 'USB board (Linux) or an SPI bridge via meshtasticd; Wi-Fi boards are bound by address in a later task', or add the route in the L6/agent task and keep the text.

minors.title: Binding present but meshmud binary missing reads as `meshtastic_unbound` ('set up with the agent') (builder's recorded deviation)
minors.where: src/daemon/services/mod.rs meshtastic(): `ChildDisplay::Absent if m.board.is_some()`; MeshmudFacts has no installed flag
minors.why: The row tells the user to set up a board that is already bound; the real cause is a missing binary (install/upgrade problem). Not M1's file; the lead should route it.
minors.fix: Add `installed: bool` to MeshmudFacts (mod.rs facts() has cfg.meshmud_installed()) and map Absent+bound+!installed to an ERROR/NOT SET reason 'meshmud not installed'.

minors.title: Flow tests silently SKIP (and pass) when python3 is absent
minors.where: tests/api_v1_meshtastic.rs harness(): `eprintln!("python3 not found ... SKIPPED"); return None`
minors.why: On a CI box without python3 the six flow tests print a line and pass green, hiding regressions in identify, restart, states and the shim. check.sh does not assert python3 exists.
minors.fix: Have check.sh (or the test) fail when python3 is missing, or mark the tests #[ignore] via a build-time env check so the skip is visible in the summary.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Identify profile = restart policy whose first exit is final (crash_loop_threshold 1); the monitor swaps the exited identify-born child for a service-policy child on its next tick
deviation_verdicts.why: Spec-compatible with 'never a second open': the supervisor's record_exit returns Degraded on the first exit so it never respawns; swap_identify_child only runs when state == Degraded (process already reaped), stop_and_wait joins the old handle, then one spawn. ChildControl::restart on the identify-born child respawns without touching the policy and still one process at a time. The only timing difference is a 0-2 s respawn instead of the 2 s back-off once; the service policy applies after that. Verified by reading supervise.rs spawn_child and the swap test (kill9 -> Degraded, no respawn, swap, then supervisor respawn).

deviation_verdicts.deviation: MeshtasticConfig.dev_root (production `/`) for the serial-uplink presence check
deviation_verdicts.why: Test seam only; uplink_present joins dev_root with the validated path, meshmud always opens the real path from the rendered config. No production behaviour change.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: registry.rs keeps an absent store entry that holds a Meshtastic binding (previously deleted when it had no summary)
deviation_verdicts.why: A binding is configuration; dropping it on a tick would silently unbind a Wi-Fi board. Bounded: at most one binding survives sanitize() and gc() exempts only bound entries. forget still clears it.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: The identify route runs the step in a spawned task so a client disconnect never cancels it mid-probe
deviation_verdicts.why: Fail-closed: every branch of identify() (spawn failure, exit 3, meshmud death, reader timeout/malformed, transfer failure) calls abort()/release_for; a dropped request future would have left meshmud running with the port claimed. Minor side effect recorded above: shutdown waits for the step.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Facts.meshmud.channel_utilization is always null
deviation_verdicts.why: Honest null rather than a fabricated value: the reader excludes the local board, so the daemon has no board-reported utilisation; per-node utilisation is still in Nearby. The detail field exists per §14. A later reader change can fill it without a spec edit.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: GET /api/v1/fromradio returns exactly one frame per call whatever `all=` says
deviation_verdicts.why: The firmware's all=true concatenates protobufs with no delimiter (unparseable as separate messages); the official transport-http defaults to receiveBatchRequests=false and loops until an empty body, which this serves correctly. Must be confirmed against the pinned web bundle at panel build (open question kept).

deviation_verdicts.deviation: No route binds a Wi-Fi board by address; openapi text says 'USB or Wi-Fi board'
deviation_verdicts.why: D20(a) scopes the identify route to the Meshtastic step on detected boards; address binding is an agent/L6 task. The daemon does render and run a TCP binding found in devices.json (tested). The contract text must be amended (minor above) so the copy stays honest.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Binding present but meshmud binary missing reports child Absent with board set -> services rule reads `meshtastic_unbound`
deviation_verdicts.why: Recorded honestly with the right fix location (services/mod.rs, not M1's files). Nothing opens or claims a port; the row is merely mislabelled. Tracked as a minor for the lead to route.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Identifying a second board while one is bound returns 409 port_busy on the downlink
deviation_verdicts.why: Follows §14 directly: one meshmud, one 127.0.0.1:11230 downlink. The 409 detail names `meshmud`; forget-then-identify is the documented path.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Presence hygiene beyond the spec: meshtastic.json deleted on unbind and before the reader spawns; file read only while a board is bound
deviation_verdicts.why: Strictly fail-closed: an old or foreign node DB can never make the service LIVE or feed Nearby for a different board. remove_file never follows a symlink; the reader rewrites atomically.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: attach_panels relies on P1's PanelHost::revocations() and report_dropped()
deviation_verdicts.why: Compiles against the landed P1 API; the drop count also reaches panel.state through with_dropped independently. A rename is a compile error, not a silent break.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Shim defaults not in the spec: 16 sessions, 1024-frame queue, 60 s idle
deviation_verdicts.why: All bounded: <= 1024 x 512 B = 512 KiB per viewer, <= 8 MiB total; 60 s idle is far above the official client's poll interval. The spec asks only for capacity-bounded drop-oldest with a surfaced drop count, which this is.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Presence unit test uses the mkfifo command instead of unsafe libc::mkfifo
deviation_verdicts.why: Test-only; coreutils mkfifo is on every CI image the suite already assumes (sh, stat, sleep, kill).

deviation_verdicts.deviation: tests/api_v1_meshtastic.rs skips its flow tests (SKIP line) when python3 is absent
deviation_verdicts.why: Reasonable for a dev box, but a silent green on CI hides regressions; tracked as a minor (make the skip loud or fail check.sh without python3).

result.notes:
Read first: (1) identify.rs:199-265 and registry.rs record_identify side by side -- the major is the ordering: service installed and claims transferred before record_identify, and record_identify flushes the store before it checks `published`; a forget in the probe window persists a binding on a forgotten (hidden) entry. (2) shim.rs read_loop/session() for the two small shim minors. (3) tests/api_v1_meshtastic.rs:1680 for the flake (test-side only; reproduced 10/36 under 32 CPU hogs, every failure at that line; the product shim is not racing).

Verified sound against the lens: GPL boundary is clean (no Cargo.toml change, no protobuf crate; the shim handles only the 4-byte 0x94 0xC3 len stream header; the reader is a separate python process via -I; meshmud a separate binary). Config rendering: serial pattern anchored and additionally refuses `.`/`..`, host validated as IP literal or RFC 1123 name, TOML produced by the serializer, one loopback TCP downlink only, advertise=false, atomic_write creates the temp file O_EXCL with mode 0600 (never world-readable even briefly) in a 0700 dir; a hand-edited devices.json uplink is revalidated on load and again in render_config, so no unvalidated string reaches meshmud's open. Presence ingest: O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK|O_CLOEXEC, fstat on the fd (no path TOCTOU), <= 1 MiB checked before and after the read, schema 1, <= 4096 nodes, duplicate nums refused, id must equal `!`+num, typed ranges, pubkey 44-char base64 (the `s[..43]` slice is safe because the last byte is '='), names stripped of control/bidi/invisible then cut on a char boundary to 40 bytes, invalid keeps last + counter; a missing file clears. Identify: consent checked before any lookup; PortTable claim for both the uplink and the downlink; every failure branch (spawn fail, reader exit 3, meshmud exit caught by the 50 ms watch, timeout with kill_on_drop, malformed output, transfer failure) stops the child and releases the claims; transfer is atomic in the table; the swap never runs two meshmuds. Shim: dispatch is only reachable after the listener validated the p111 cookie session (listener.rs:156-177; no cookie -> 401), the key is the server-side session id, queues are per key; framing strict with max 512, partial reads and noise handled, deframer buffer bounded (~4 KiB + 516), revocation and Lagged close sessions, idle close works. Restart = [meshmud, meshtastic-presence] in order; shutdown joins both and releases claims. No wall-clock in ordering (Instant/ticks only); no secrets in logs or Problem details; no panics found on peer input (checked every index/slice/cast).

Open questions for the owner: (a) confirm at panel build that the pinned Meshtastic web bundle's HTTP transport polls /fromradio until an empty body with all=false (default receiveBatchRequests=false) -- one frame per call is safe either way but a client that relies on all=true batching would be slow, not broken; (b) DTR/RTS on meshmud's serial open remains a hardware-test gate (research note 24); (c) the §14 path pattern admits any `/dev/<name>` (e.g. /dev/zero, /dev/sda) -- harmless as the daemon user, but if the owner wants the pattern narrowed to tty*/serial/by-id it is a spec edit, not an M1 bug; (d) Nearby label falls back to the device name ('heard via Meshtastic on Likely: Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 V3') -- U1 copy may prefer the alias-or-hw_model.

Check command: cargo stages green here as well (fmt/clippy/musl checks were green in the builder's run; I rebuilt and ran tests/api_v1_meshtastic.rs 8/8 and the meshtastic+ports unit tests 23/23 in a private target dir). Nothing was edited, staged or committed.

result.task: U1: UI data layer + Messages + Contacts (commit 858077f, os/interface/ui)

majors.title: 'ignore' on a message request is a DELETE, but §7.2 says an ignored request is kept
majors.where: src/views/messages/requests.tsx:36-37 (act('ignore') -> adapter.contacts.forget), copy at requests.tsx:1-4 and model.ts:216; mock + test encode the same reading (test/messaging-mock.test.ts:152)
majors.why: §7.2 says the user ignores and the request is 'kept in the request list, never auto-pruned while pending, no ACK sent'. The contract says the same: Thread.request is 'accept or leave it pending'. Here 'ignore' calls DELETE /contacts/{id}, and F1's fabric.rs forget() then calls store.request_remove. Concrete sequence: (1) the INTRO from peer P is held, with no ACK. (2) The user clicks ignore, then Yes. (3) The request and its held words are discarded (the mock drops the thread too), and the UI announces 'Ignored the request from P'. (4) P was never ACKed, so it keeps its copy (§9: kept until delivered) and retransmits on its next link event. (5) A fresh request from P appears. So the ignore does not last, the copy is false, and the held messages the spec says are kept are lost.
majors.fix: Make 'ignore' leave the request pending, with no DELETE: collapse it under an 'ignored' fold. If discarding is wanted, offer it as a separately labelled 'forget request' with honest copy ('if they write again it comes back'). The owner decides whether the contract gains an `ignored` flag so ignored requests can leave the attention count.

minors.title: Camera stays on if the jsQR chunk fails to load
minors.why: Promise.all([loadDecoder(), getUserMedia()]) rejects as soon as import('jsqr') fails. Example: a tab left open across a node update, so the old chunk hash returns 404. catch() then calls stop() while `stream` is still null. The getUserMedia promise resolves later, after the user clicks Allow, and nothing ever stops its tracks. The camera stays live with no preview until the tab closes, and the page says 'The camera could not be started'. This breaks the file's own claim that the camera is released when the dialog closes.
minors.fix: Await loadDecoder() before calling getUserMedia. Alternatively, keep the media promise and stop its tracks in catch/stop when it resolves after stop.

minors.title: An older thread response can overwrite a newer one
minors.where: src/lib/api/store.ts:544 loadThread (callers: useThread effect, onSent, retry, refreshAll at :431)
minors.why: Concurrent loadThread calls for the same peer are not ordered; whichever response arrives last replaces the slot. Example: a reset triggers refreshAll and load L0, then the user sends and onSent issues L1. If L0 resolves after L1, the page loses the just-sent message. A message that stays `queued` (no path) gets no further frame, so it stays missing from the thread until the next reload. A state can also step back from delivered to sent.
minors.fix: Add a per-peer request generation and drop stale responses, or merge by id and never lower stateRank.

minors.title: An open conversation grows without bound from message frames
minors.why: The page is loaded as the newest `limit` messages (100). Every later `message` frame appends with no cap, so a long-lived tab on a chatty thread keeps every message in memory. Only a reset reload restores the window.
minors.fix: After an upsert, trim to the page's limit (drop the oldest, set more=true).

minors.title: reuse() is O(n²) with JSON.stringify, now run on threads and contacts
minors.where: src/lib/api/store.ts:114 (used by refreshThreads/refreshContacts on every message/contact frame)
minors.why: For each new record, prev.find(sameJson) stringifies both sides. Measured with 400-character last lines: 100 threads take 13 ms, 300 take 100 ms and 600 take 386 ms per refresh on desktop; phones are several times slower. Anyone who can reach the node can push the thread count up to the 256 pending-request quota with INTROs, which turns every incoming message into visible jank.
minors.fix: Index prev by peer/node_id and compare only the record with the same key.

minors.title: The picture-file cap limits bytes, not pixels
minors.why: A 12 MB PNG can declare 40000x40000 highly compressible pixels. createImageBitmap(file) decodes it at full size (gigabytes of RGBA) before fitScale applies, so a crafted picture the user picks can exhaust memory or crash the tab.
minors.fix: Read the image dimensions first (img.decode() plus a naturalWidth/Height check) and refuse anything above a pixel cap, or decode with createImageBitmap(file, {resizeWidth, resizeHeight}) after a header check.

minors.title: A custody REJECT_UNKNOWN_DEST shows the wrong reason sentence
minors.why: F1 maps REJECT_UNKNOWN_DEST to state `sent` with reason_code `hub_not_yours`. The UI always shows the queued sentence 'it is delivered when you meet directly', where §9 says 'your hub does not know them'. Advanced also says 'frame written to a link'. Known codes override the daemon's own sentence, so a corrected daemon `reason` would still be hidden.
minors.fix: Key the reason copy on (state, code): sent with hub_not_yours reads 'Your hub does not know them…'. Have C1 add a distinct code.

minors.title: Lookup tables are plain objects, so the 'unknown renders unknown' rule has holes
minors.where: src/views/messages/model.ts:45 glyphFor, :50 stateCopy, :55 reasonText (`in`); lib/api/contacts.ts:260 roleLabels
minors.why: A state or reason_code such as 'constructor' or 'toString' resolves to Object.prototype members. The glyph label is undefined and reasonText returns a function, which React renders as nothing (with a warning). These values come from the daemon, not a peer, so the risk is low, but the U1b rule is not kept.
minors.fix: Use Object.hasOwn() or a Map for STATE_COPY, GLYPHS, REASON_COPY and ROLE_LABEL.

minors.title: Advanced omits the §16 'path' and the omission is not recorded; the 'evidence:' line restates the state
minors.why: §16 says 'Advanced appends: raw msg_id, path, custody receipts'. The contract has no path field, but this gap is not among the recorded deviations. The receipts line is labelled 'evidence:' although it only restates the state definition, so an Advanced reader may think a receipt was inspected.
minors.fix: Record the path gap for C1. Relabel the line to 'what this state means:'.

minors.title: The attention badge counts requests but links to a page that does not list them
minors.why: When a message request is the only pending item, the badge shows 1 and links to Overview's 'Needs you' block, which lists no requests (needsYou() takes no contacts). It is a dead end: the U1 row asks for the badge to count requests, and the user cannot find what is counted.
minors.fix: Have the Overview owner add an 'N message requests -> /messages' row, or point the badge at /messages when requests are the only items.

minors.title: The agent goal is wrong for two fabric states
minors.why: The daemon reports hub_unreachable as NOT SET, so the banner offers 'Set up messaging' and its enroll question. §16 puts hub unreachable under messaging.fix. hub_waiting (a hub with 0 members) also gets 'Set up… enrolling with a home hub', but §15 reserves set-up-to-enroll for a member; a hub should be offered 'Let a node use this hub'.
minors.fix: Choose the goal and question by reason_code (hub_unreachable -> fix; hub_waiting -> offer copy) until U2's messaging.* goals land.

minors.title: The forget copy is not what F1 does
minors.why: F1 (fabric.rs notes) keeps a forgotten contact's undelivered outgoing messages queued as waiting_for_key, and lists the peer again as a key-less contact after a restart. The copy only says that their keys are dropped and history stays, so a user expects the forget to be final.
minors.fix: Add 'Messages still waiting to go out stay in the outbox, and bring them back as a contact without keys after a restart.' Alternatively, have F1 tombstone the outbox on forget.

minors.title: The add-contact result sentence misreports known and pending peers
minors.why: `before` comes from the store's contacts, which include requests. Pasting the id of a pending requester says '<label> is already a contact. Nothing changed.' and offers 'Write to them' to a read-only thread. When the contacts list never loaded (null), an already-known contact reads 'Added …'.
minors.fix: Branch on the returned contact.request ('they already wrote to you; accept the request') and treat a null list as unknown.

minors.title: Peer text has no direction isolation and is uncleaned in the Advanced raw block
minors.why: Persian or Arabic messages render in an LTR paragraph, which misplaces punctuation and digits; the builder explicitly cares about Persian. The Advanced raw JSON block shows m.text as JSON.stringify output, which does not escape U+202E or U+2066, so overrides stripped everywhere else reorder that line.
minors.fix: Put dir="auto" on bubbles and previews. Map cleanPeerText over the text fields of the raw block, or escape bidi controls in prettyJson.

minors.title: The per-message disclosure departs from the shared Disclosure (DESIGN)
minors.why: It is a custom <details> with the marker hidden, no '>'/'v' glyph, no FOCUS_RING and min-h-8 (32 px), where every other view uses components/disclosure (44 px target, visible state, focus ring). Sighted users get no visible cue that the time line opens.
minors.fix: Use <Disclosure> or copy its marker, focus ring and min-h-11.

minors.title: The card text check differs from the daemon's parser
minors.why: The daemon (mesh111 contacts.rs parse_card_text) ignores trailing '=', is case-insensitive and caps the raw text at 512 bytes. The UI refuses padded text with 'letters and digits only' and accepts up to 2048 characters after stripping, so a valid padded card is refused locally. The pasted text is not capped before the regex runs; 5 MB took about 7 ms in my run, so this is fine for now.
minors.fix: Strip '=' with whitespace and dashes, and cap the raw input at 512 (plus slack), matching MAX_CARD_TEXT.

minors.title: Vector tests are hand-copied and one test asserts the rejected reading
minors.why: The KATs and negatives are copied by hand rather than loaded from os/identity/test-vectors/encoding.json. All 8 hex negatives and 3 bech32 negatives (64-byte payload, test1, nsec1, '1qqq…') are missing. I ran the full JSON through parseNodeId: every KAT decodes and every negative is refused, so the code is right but the test can drift. The mock test 'ignoring discards the request and its held messages' encodes the DELETE reading of ignore, not the spec.
minors.fix: Import encoding.json in the test. Rewrite the ignore test to assert that the request stays pending with no outgoing frame.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Budget gate red (255.3 KB vs 200 KB)
deviation_verdicts.why: Right call not to touch the gate. It is now resolved by D21 (9bd854e). Against D21, U1 passes: my private build gives eager 101.2 KB, lazy 154.2 KB, largest lazy chunk jsQR 47.5 KB (under 64). jsQR is reached only by dynamic import from the contacts chunk; index.html has no modulepreload links; no mock fixtures are in dist.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Request 'ignore' = DELETE /contacts/{id} behind a confirm
deviation_verdicts.why: §7.2 ('kept in the request list, never auto-pruned while pending, no ACK sent') and the contract's Thread.request ('accept or leave it pending') both require ignore to leave the request pending. DELETE discards the held messages, and the INTRO comes back on the sender's next retransmission. See the major.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Agent hand-off via questionPrompt with setup/fix goals until U2
deviation_verdicts.why: Verified that no peer text enters the prompt. It holds two fixed question strings plus buildPrompt's context: the fabric ServiceRecord (daemon booleans, numbers and sentences; detail is store/hub/member facts) and status. The goal choice for hub_unreachable and hub_waiting is off (see minors).

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Advanced 'custody receipts' derived from state + reason (no receipt bytes in the API)
deviation_verdicts.why: It never claims bytes it does not have, so it is honest. Two caveats: the 'evidence:' label reads as inspection of a receipt (relabel it), and §16 'path' is also missing but unrecorded.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Edited store/hooks/flash-model tests for openRequests and the 9-service registry
deviation_verdicts.why: The tests are under test/** (U1-owned), and the changes are additive field and count updates; all 858 tests pass.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Mock ports corrected (panel 11240->11190, hub tcp-lan 11190->11183)
deviation_verdicts.why: Verified against the spec §2 ports table (dashboard 11180, tcp-lan 11183, panels 11190–11229, meshmud 11230) and the contract Panel.port bounds; the mock's meshmud downlink is 11230.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: cleanPeerText keeps ZWNJ/ZWJ and LRM/RLM; strips C0/C1, U+2028/9, BOM and U+202A–202E/U+2066–2069
deviation_verdicts.why: Explicit embeddings, overrides and isolates are removed, and implicit marks cannot override; this is needed for Persian, Arabic and emoji. Add dir=auto and clean the Advanced raw block (see minors).

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Header badge links to Overview, whose needs-you list lacks requests
deviation_verdicts.why: Disclosed honestly, and the files belong to another owner. It is still a user-visible dead end; listed as a minor for the Overview owner or as a badge-href fix.

result.notes:
Read first:
1. src/views/messages/requests.tsx:30-46 together with spec §7.2 (the major).
2. src/views/contacts/scanner.tsx:26-67 (camera leak).
3. src/lib/api/store.ts:544 loadThread and :114 reuse.

Everything else is copy or robustness.

Check run (typecheck, test, build):
- typecheck clean; 30 files / 858 tests green.
- Build ok into a private outDir. D21 budget PASS: eager 101.2 / lazy 154.2 KB, jsQR 47.5 KB under the 64 KB per-chunk cap.
- Under the old 200 KB grand total it was 255.4.

What holds:
- Peer strings never reach an href, src, attribute or prompt sink. Hrefs are built only from daemon NodeIds via hrefTo; peer text goes only into React text children.
- No dangerouslySetInnerHTML; no linkify or markdown on message text.
- Received vs claimed time follows §4: 'received'/'written' label, sender claim only inside the details, marked unverified.
- Ordering is local_seq only; wall clock is display-only.
- Requests are never auto-accepted: the composer is gated, and read_seq is never sent for a request.
- bech32: every KAT and every negative in encoding.json decodes or is refused correctly (I ran the full file through parseNodeId); 5 MB of garbage pasted in takes about 7 ms and does not throw.
- The camera is offered only when both the hostname is loopback/HTTPS (isLoopbackHost: localhost, *.localhost, 127/8, ::1) AND window.isSecureContext.
- jsQR loads only on the first scan or file pick.
- The own-card QR is drawn from the validated {size, rows} with a quiet zone in hex tokens (dark-only theme, so the plate is light).

Open questions for the owner:
- (a) Ignore semantics. Should the contract grow `ContactPatch.ignore`/`Contact.ignored`, so ignored requests stay pending and listed but leave the attention count? Or is ignore a server no-op with a UI fold, in which case the badge keeps counting? Should a 'discard request' DELETE exist at all, given the INTRO comes back on the next retransmission?
- (b) 'Accepting never ACKs more than the messages shown': ContactPatch.accept carries no seq bound, and the Messages list offers accept beside a single 140-character preview. Does the contract need `accept_up_to_seq`?
- (c) F1 reuses hub_not_yours for REJECT_UNKNOWN_DEST and emits not_enrolled/cancelled outside the contract set. C1 should add distinct codes.

Environment note: `pnpm store status` reports 23 mutated packages (react-dom, vite, vitest, wouter…). This predates U1, and a `pnpm install --force` sanity pass at some point would be prudent.

result.task: P1 — hosted panels in node111, commit 79ca52d (os/bootstrap/crates/node111/src/daemon/panels/**, dashboard/api_v1/panels.rs, dashboard/routes.rs, tests/api_v1_panels.rs); lens: web security of a multi-origin host behind one daemon

minors.title: Same-site GET from any other origin on the host drives a panel's /api/* with the victim's cookie (GET-only, opaque response)
minors.where: /home/kia/projects/111network/os/bootstrap/crates/node111/src/daemon/panels/guard.rs:183-191 (check) and listener.rs:151 (the guard never sees the path)
minors.why: The guard accepts `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site` for every path and only checks Origin/Referer on non-GET/upgrade/SSE, exactly as §13 words it. Same-site = same scheme + host, port ignored, so the dashboard origin (:11180), another panel (:11191) or any other HTTP service on the node that a browser visits is same-site with the panel, and SameSite=Strict still attaches `p111_meshtastic`. Concrete: a page on http://127.0.0.1:11180 (or :8080) runs `fetch('http://127.0.0.1:11190/api/v1/fromradio',{mode:'no-cors',credentials:'include'})` or just ``; the browser sends the cookie + `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site`; guard passes (GET), session found, shim `fromradio` pops the next FromRadio frame (meshtastic/shim.rs:385-395) — that frame is gone for the real panel. Cannot read the response (CORS stripped) and cannot write (PUT needs Origin == authority), so it is a drain/DoS of the one panel session, needing a second local origin first. Spec-compatible as built; worth closing because the fix is 3 lines and zero legitimate traffic is same-site on an API path (the panel's own JS is same-origin; only the iframe/tab navigation is same-site and it never targets /api).
minors.fix: Pass the request path into guard::check and, when static_files::is_api_path(path) and a Sec-Fetch-Site header is present, refuse anything but `same-origin`; add a test that `GET /api/v1/fromradio` with `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site` is 403 while `GET /` with it stays 200.

minors.title: Mint doc says a bearer-only caller gets 401; on trusted loopback the agent's bearer (or any local process) mints
minors.why: `mint_binding` returns the implicit loopback binding whenever `trusted_loopback` is true, before looking at credentials, so with a bearer on desktop Linux the agent gets a ticket, can swap it (peer class loopback) and PUT /api/v1/toradio with a forged `Origin` — a radio transmit without a proposal (§18.9). Under D16(a) any loopback process is already the user and could open meshmud's TCP downlink directly, so no new capability is granted and this is acceptable; but the module doc is false on trusted loopback and the API-level story for §18.9 is weaker than it needs to be. On Termux (untrusted loopback) bearer-only is correctly refused.
minors.fix: In mint_binding, return None when `auth::bearer_tokens(headers)` is non-empty (bearer callers never mint), and keep the doc line; or, if the owner wants the agent to open panels, change the doc and record it in TASKS.md.

minors.title: Integration test harness port race: panel bind fails with EADDRINUSE under parallel tests and the test talks to a sibling fixture's listener
minors.why: `free_port()` binds :0, drops it, and returns the number; with 12 tests on 4 threads another fixture can bind the same port first. Observed 1 in 4 parallel runs: `111 daemon: panel listener 127.0.0.1:34695 failed: Address already in use`, then `ticket_flow_spent_ticket_and_remint` panicked at :386 (`403 panel_ticket_expired` instead of 303) because its ticket GET reached a different fixture's panel on that port. The builder also saw flakiness (attributed to M1's test). Not a product bug; it makes check.sh red at random.
minors.fix: After `set_enabled`, assert `host.bound_addrs(ServiceId::Meshtastic)` is non-empty and retry the fixture with a fresh port (bounded), or hand the fixture a 40-wide block and read the real bound port from `bound_addrs`.

minors.title: Static serving reads and sha256-hashes the whole file per request (no cache), and the API-path check runs on the encoded path
minors.why: Every GET of a bundle file allocates the file (≤ 64 MiB) and hashes it; a session holder with 128 concurrent GETs of the largest bundle asset holds 128× that in memory and burns CPU. Only authenticated clients reach it, so it is a nuisance, not a hole (builder's note c). Separately, `/%61pi/v1/x` decodes to an API path but `is_api_path` sees the raw path, so it gets the SPA fallback — harmless (the shim matches literal paths) but the module doc's 'never under an API path' is not strictly true.
minors.fix: Derive the ETag from (len, mtime_ns, ino) or cache per path keyed by mtime and stream the body (ReaderStream); evaluate is_api_path on the decoded rel path as well and answer the problem 404 there.

minors.title: Listener limits are global per listener and the idle timer is per byte, so one peer can hold every slot or trickle a body for hours
minors.why: `max_conns` 128 has no per-peer share: with LAN on, one LAN host can open 128 idle connections and refresh them every <60 s, and the legit browser gets its SYNs closed. A session holder can send a PUT /api/v1/toradio with an 8 MiB Content-Length one byte per 59 s (each byte touches the activity clock) and hold a slot for days. Header-read (10 s, hyper 1.12 re-arms it per request so keep-alive idle is covered) and the 60 s activity idle are correctly in place; this is the remaining slow-body/slot-exhaustion residual. Same class as the main dashboard listener, which still has no timeouts at all (pre-existing, builder's note e).
minors.fix: Wrap the shim body read in `tokio::time::timeout` (absolute per-request deadline, e.g. 30 s) and add a small per-peer-IP connection cap (e.g. 16) in `serve`; consider giving the main listener the same header-read/idle timeouts in a follow-up.

minors.title: Trusted-loopback binding stores a hash of the ~39-bit pair code; brute-forceable to the live code if the file or a Binding ever leaks
minors.why: `pair_epoch` = sha256('111 panel epoch v1\0' || code) over an 8-char/30-symbol code (≈2^39): offline inversion is minutes on a GPU. Today it lives only in state/panel-sessions.json (0600, same class as dashboard-pair.json which holds the code in clear) and in memory, and nothing serves `PanelSessionRec`, so there is no new exposure; it is a footgun for any future diagnostics route or log line that prints a session record.
minors.fix: Bind to a random 32-byte per-generation nonce written beside the pair file on rotate (or keep the hash but mark `Binding` `#[serde(skip)]` for anything other than the session file and note the sensitivity in the doc).

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Main-listener 308 (Host: localhost → 127.0.0.1) skips /health and /api/status
deviation_verdicts.why: Both are Layer 1 machine contracts pinned by tests/dashboard_http.rs, unauthenticated GETs with no state change and no panel/ticket involvement; curl does not follow redirects. Exemption is exact-path, Host guard runs first (routes.rs layer order), [::1] bracketed and served. Safe.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Origin/Referer authority enforced on every non-GET/upgrade/SSE (not only when Sec-Fetch-* is absent); unknown Sec-Fetch-Site, TRACE/CONNECT, missing/repeated Host refused
deviation_verdicts.why: Strict superset of §13, fail closed; a panel's own JS is same-origin and fetch always sends Origin on non-GET, so nothing legitimate is refused. Verified by guard unit tests and host_and_origin_matrix.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: 'Enabled' = registered ∧ bundle dir exists ∧ registry state ≠ unset; mint for a non-enabled panel is 404 not_found
deviation_verdicts.why: Fail-closed reading of an implicit spec term; matches the contract's 'or its service is not set up'. Note `error`/`starting` still count as set up, which is fine (the listener answers 502 upstream_error through the shim). Disable drops listener, tickets and sessions (reconcile).

deviation_verdicts.deviation: 401 unauthenticated without cookie/ticket; a ticket on a non-GET/HEAD is burned and answered 403; the swap is a 303 to entry.path with no-store
deviation_verdicts.why: §13 only defines 403 panel_ticket_expired for spent/expired tickets; 401 is the existing contract code for 'no credential'. Burning on any presentation matches 'spent on any method'. 303 + no-store is the right redirect for a GET swap and the policy headers are applied to it too.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Trusted-loopback mints bound to a hash of the current pair code; rotate (manual or the 20-failure auto-rotation) revokes them
deviation_verdicts.why: There is no s111 session on trusted loopback, and §13 requires revocation on `111 dashboard rotate`; binding to the pair generation gives exactly that and is checked per request (binding_alive), so no window. The auto-rotation side effect (a LAN attacker failing 20 pairs logs the owner's panel sessions out) is a nuisance, fail-closed, and already the pair-code policy. See minor 6 on the hash's brute-forceability.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: LAN-off revocation happens at daemon start (sessions minted with LAN on, or from non-loopback peers, dropped)
deviation_verdicts.why: D16(b): lan_enabled is read once per lifetime, so LAN-off only ever takes effect at a start; revoking there is the earliest honest moment and errs on the side of dropping. Verified by revocation_on_rotate_disable_and_lan_off and the ticket store unit test.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Mint adds 400 bad_request when the dashboard Host cannot address a panel and 403 loopback_only for a loopback-only panel from a non-loopback dashboard host
deviation_verdicts.why: Both are additive refusals using existing contract codes; the alternative is minting a ticket URL that can never work (loopback-only listeners never bind LAN).

deviation_verdicts.deviation: With a valid session, any Upgrade request is 400; manifests with [proxy] websocket/sse = true are not registered
deviation_verdicts.why: D20(a): the generic proxy with WebSocket/SSE is reserved for P7; refusing the upgrade and the manifest is the fail-closed form of 'not built'. The guard still applies the Origin check to upgrades/SSE before that, as §13 asks.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Manifest strictness: [frame] sandbox only 'default', [license] served only 'unmodified', [health] url only loopback http with multi_client = true and not probed in v1
deviation_verdicts.why: Unknown values ⇒ unregistered is §13's own rule; the shipped meshtastic.toml passes; health=url reading 'unknown' rather than probing is honest for v1 and the LISTEN probe (never a connect) is what the Meshtastic declaration uses.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Panel listeners also bind [::1] best effort; a failed IPv4 bind retries after 30 s
deviation_verdicts.why: Mirrors the dashboard's bind plan exactly; the disable→re-enable rebind gap (builder's b) is ≤ 30 s and fail-closed (no listener, mint still succeeds but the frame shows nothing until retry). Could be shortened later by awaiting the aborted serve task before rebinding.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: daemon/mod.rs and api_v1/mod.rs registrations shared with M1 (landed in 99f5e0a)
deviation_verdicts.why: Verified at HEAD: PanelHost::load gets dashboard.api.lan_enabled, provider feeds the registry, panels::spawn runs the 2 s reconcile, meshtastic.attach_panels forwards revocations to the shim; panels::router() is merged before the require_session route_layer and under csrf_guard (api_v1/mod.rs:227-250), so GET /panels needs a session and the mint POST needs JSON + Origin == Host.

result.notes: Read first: the task is sound; no majors. The one thing I would land before lock is minor 1 (3-line Fetch-Metadata tightening on /api paths) together with the harness race (minor 3) — both small; the rest can ride the next wave. Lens answers: (1) read a panel's /api from another origin — no (every Access-Control-* stripped on every answer incl. refusals; OPTIONS/TRACE/CONNECT 403; cookie SameSite=Strict+HttpOnly host-only); drive it — cross-site never (Sec-Fetch-Site refused before the swap/session), same-site non-GET never (Origin/Referer must equal host:port), same-site GET yes with the victim's cookie (minor 1; spec-permitted; for Meshtastic that dequeues frames). (2) ticket: 128-bit from getrandom, kept only as sha256, Instant-based 30 s, single use (`take` removes on any presentation, incl. non-GET and cookie-present), bound to panel + peer class (loopback class / exact remote IP) + minting binding, checked alive at swap; no URI is logged anywhere under dashboard/ or panels/ (grepped eprintln!/println!/TraceLayer) — the ticket exists only in the mint response body (no-store) and on the panel port; the 308 middleware never sees panel URLs, so `redact_ticket` is dead code until an access log exists. (3) sessions file: atomic_write = O_EXCL tmp + fchmod 0600 + fsync + rename + dir fsync; read refuses symlinks/non-regular/>1 MiB and garbled ⇒ empty; revocation is evaluated per request in `session_for` via `binding_alive` (auth.sessions() filtered by max age; pair epoch for loopback), so logout/rotate/forget-companion take effect on the very next request — the 2 s sweep only persists and broadcasts; disable aborts the serve task (JoinSet drop closes every open connection) and revokes; LAN-off at start. No window found. (4) static: single percent-decode, %2F/%5C/%00/control/dot segments refused, canonical containment after symlink resolution (unit test with /etc symlinks), SPA fallback never for raw /api paths (problem 404), nosniff on everything, 64 MiB cap; residual = whole-file hash per request + encoded-path nit (minor 4). (5) hyper 1.12 header_read_timeout 10 s (re-armed per request head so keep-alive idle is covered), activity idle 60 s, 128-conn cap, Content-Length pre-check + to_bytes cap 8 MiB (413 before the shim); residual = no per-peer cap and per-byte idle (minor 5). (6) every panel answer carries `frame-ancestors http://<accepted host>:11180 http://<accepted host>:80` (or 'none' when no accepted host), XFO dropped, upstream CSP frame-ancestors stripped; a LAN origin http://192.168.1.9 cannot frame http://192.168.1.5:11190 (not listed, and the navigation is cross-site ⇒ refused before any body); dashboard CSP has no frame-src by default so panels are framable only when enabled and listening (fail closed). (7) exemptions safe. (8) Termux: trusted_loopback false ⇒ mint needs an s111 cookie (bearer-only 401) and the panel needs ticket/cookie regardless — verified by untrusted_loopback_still_needs_the_ticket and the code path. (9) agent bearer on trusted loopback minting: acceptable under D16(a)+D20(e) — the bearer grants nothing beyond what any loopback process already has (incl. meshmud's loopback TCP downlink), and it is refused on Termux; but the module doc claims bearer-only ⇒ 401, so either make mint_binding refuse bearer callers (my recommendation, keeps §18.9 honest at the API) or fix the doc and record the choice. Open questions for the owner/lead: (a) does §13's 'header-read and idle timeouts on every listener' include the main dashboard listener? It has none (pre-existing; builder's e) — if yes, a follow-up task on dashboard/mod.rs. (b) Should the 20-failed-pairs auto-rotation also log the node owner's trusted-loopback panel sessions out (it does today; fail-closed, nuisance-only)? Runs: `cargo test -p node111 --test api_v1_panels` 12/12 ×3 parallel + ×1 single-threaded (first parallel run hit the port race once); `--lib panels::` 25/25; `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p node111 --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean at HEAD (includes M1/U1). Tests assert the spec (ticket shape/TTL/single use/peer binding, cookie attributes, no CORS ever, Host/Origin matrix, 308 shape, policy headers on every answer kind, SPA vs API, per-host CSP, loopback-only bind, Termux, revocation on rotate/logout/disable/LAN-off); nothing asserts an implementation detail that would resist the fixes above.

result.task: F1 — mesh111 runtime (commit c8a093c): links (tcp-lan + lossy), frag Tier 0/1, outbox/ACK, contacts, mailbox member+hub, fabric actor

majors.title: Unbounded actor input queue: an unauthenticated LAN peer can OOM the daemon
majors.where: src/fabric.rs:569 (`mpsc::unbounded_channel()` for `Input`) + `Core::add_link` recv forwarder (~fabric.rs:1226-1243), which drains tcp_lan.rs:292's bounded (1024) inbound channel into the unbounded one
majors.why: Any LAN host completes hello + a self-signed announce (FabricGate admits every verified announce that does not collide with a pinned NodeId), then streams 88 B T_SEALED frames (MIN_PACKET_LEN) at line rate. Each frame costs the actor an X25519 + AEAD in `open_envelope` before `PairMacFailed` (tens of µs), so the actor drains ~10^4 frames/s while the forwarder enqueues 10^5–10^6/s; the `Input::Frame` backlog grows without bound (hundreds of MB/s at 1 Gbit) until the hub is OOM-killed. tcp_lan's own bound and TICK_BATCH do not help because the forwarder never blocks. Same path with 256 connections × 65 KB frames.
majors.fix: Carry frames on a bounded `mpsc::channel` with `send().await` in the forwarder (TCP back-pressure flows end to end through tcp_lan's bounded channel) and `select!` it against the API/event channel in `run`; or `try_send` + drop + `counters.dropped` when full.

majors.title: Re-enrollment skips custody already held for the member (silent non-delivery through the hub)
majors.why: Bob is enrolled and away; Alice's items land in custody at seq 10..12 (Alice shows `relayed`). Bob restores his identity on a new device, or simply re-scans a fresh offer, and re-enrolls: the hub answers floor = 12, Bob's cursor becomes 12, MAILBOX_FETCH {12} returns nothing. Items 10..12 are never streamed, stay uncommitted at the hub until capacity, and Alice's copies sit at `relayed` ('a mailbox node saved it and will hold it for them') until a direct meeting. The floor only ever has an effect on re-enrollment, where it loses mail.
majors.fix: In `on_enroll` answer floor = (lowest uncommitted custody_seq for that dest) − 1 when any is held, else `custody_high()` (one query); keep the member's max() semantics.

minors.title: `heard` grows per verified sender, including refused INTROs (a trace §18.1 forbids)
minors.where: src/fabric.rs `on_sealed`: `self.heard.insert(sender)` runs before the kind dispatch and before `request_put` decides
minors.why: An attacker minting identities adds ~80 B per identity forever (a second, slower memory-growth path for the same unauthenticated peer), and a quota-refused INTRO is supposed to leave nothing but a counter.
minors.fix: Insert into `heard` only when `keys.get(&sender).is_some()` or after `request_put` returns Filed/AlreadyPending.

minors.title: `node1…` pending contacts are lost on restart (§7.2(2): 'the node stores the NodeId')
minors.where: src/fabric.rs `pending_keys` (memory) + `recover()` rebuilds only from outbox peers
minors.why: A contact added by NodeId with no queued message disappears at the next daemon restart (every update/reboot); the UI showed it with `has_key:false` and it silently vanishes. Read marks resetting is a UX annoyance; the node1 loss is user-visible data loss.
minors.fix: C3: a tiny `pending_node_ids(node_id)` table (or nullable `enc_pubkey`) written on add/forget and read in `recover`; read marks may stay in memory for v1 if documented, or ride the same migration.

minors.title: MAILBOX_COMMIT is dropped when the hub connection is gone at flush time
minors.why: If the last item arrived just before the socket died, the cursor was advanced in the store but the COMMIT is discarded; the hub keeps those items non-evict-first until the next item is processed and committed (capacity pressure on the hub, no loss).
minors.fix: Keep `commit_owed` when unsent, and send COMMIT{cursor} next to FETCH in `hub_link_up`.

minors.title: `requeue_orphans` plans for TCP instead of the destination path
minors.why: After a crash a message re-planned as one 60 KB packet can never leave on a 160 B path (`seal_data` returns None every pump; stays `queued` with no reason). v1 has only tcp-lan, so latent.
minors.fix: Use `self.plan_mtu(&peer)` (count fixed at queue time, §5).

minors.title: Hub push bookkeeping advances `high` even when the frame is never written
minors.where: src/fabric.rs `stream_items` → `send_control_keys` (`Ok(_) => {}` when sealed > room) and `on_sent(Tag::None, Err)` ignored, while `c.push.pushed(seq)` is recorded
minors.why: A skipped MAILBOX_ITEM is never re-streamed on that connection and the member's cursor jumps past it with later items. Unreachable with v1 sizes (item ≤ 65,415 + 98 B wrapper fits), reachable with an L6 hub link of a smaller MTU.
minors.fix: Record `pushed(seq)` only when the frame was queued, and roll it back on a send error.

minors.title: The announce's home-hub hint (a locator) pre-empts the hub's own verdict
minors.why: A contact who moved to our hub but whose stored announce still hints elsewhere stays `queued` forever although CUSTODY_PUT would be ACCEPTED; §7.3 says the hint is 'a locator only'.
minors.fix: Skip the pre-emption when `is_enrolled(peer)` at our hub, or use the hint only for the UI reason and let REJECT_UNKNOWN_DEST decide.

minors.title: Custody reject reason sticks after a later successful direct send
minors.why: A `sent/hub_not_yours` message written directly to the peer keeps 'your hub does not know them' until delivered.
minors.fix: On a successful Frag write with state already Sent, `set_state(id, Sent, None)`.

minors.title: Forgetting the home hub leaves `settings.home_hub` and the maintained dial
minors.why: `route()` keeps choosing the hub, `pump_hub` bails on `keys.get(hub)` every tick, the dialer keeps reconnecting; status still reports `enrolled`.
minors.fix: Clear `home_hub`, `release` the dial, `settings_changed()`.

minors.title: Claim mismatch on a dial resets back-off: a wrong `expected` redials every 500 ms forever
minors.where: src/link/tcp_lan.rs `maintain` (serve returns true after the handshake, before the fabric hangs up on the claim)
minors.why: `enroll(address)` or a hub address now answered by another node produces a permanent 2 dials/s loop with full handshakes.
minors.fix: Treat a hang-up within the first frames as a failed attempt for back-off, or `release` the target on claim mismatch in `on_link_event`.

minors.title: Thread listing scans whole histories per call
minors.why: Every `GET /threads` loads up to 1M rows per peer into memory (local-API memory spike); recorded as a C3 wish.
minors.fix: C3 newest-N query; cap the scan until then.

minors.title: Lossy test cannot tell SACK-inferred retransmits from the harness hammer
minors.where: tests/lossy.rs `drive()` (retry_all after 120 ms idle) + `tier1_over_lossy_loopback_with_loss_and_reorder` asserting only `retransmits > 0`
minors.why: A broken `infer_losses` would still pass because `retry_all` presumes everything lost.
minors.fix: Assert `retransmits > 0` before the first `retry_all`, or count inferred losses in a separate counter and assert it.

minors.title: DUPLICATE counted as `relayed` evidence is unrecorded
minors.why: §6.2 names ACCEPTED as the only evidence; DUPLICATE from the home hub does mean the item is held, so this is sound, but it is a reading the doc lists without a deviation entry.
minors.fix: Record it in the F1 readings / TASKS row.

minors.title: `cancelled` and `not_enrolled` reason codes are emitted but undocumented in the contract
minors.why: Clients render `unknown`; the field is free-form so nothing breaks, but the contract text is stale.
minors.fix: C1 follow-up: add both to the described emitted set (additive).

deviation_verdicts.deviation: §6.1 ordering as selection priority; wire order is C2's canonical ascending
deviation_verdicts.why: The spec's purpose (acked packet always acknowledged, no retransmit-forever) is kept by selection; unit test covers >8 ranges across 3 epochs and round-trips through ack.rs.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: ENROLL_OK leading status byte (0 OK / 1 mismatch / 2 refused / 3 locked out) on the same kind
deviation_verdicts.why: Fail-closed and necessary under 'no timers' (a silent refusal would hang the member); but it changes ENROLL_OK's wire layout, so §7.3/§3.2 must record it as an as-built amendment (C2 owns the registry).

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Custody rejects keep `sent`; UNKNOWN_DEST ⇒ hub_not_yours, UNENROLLED ⇒ not_enrolled (not in C1's set)
deviation_verdicts.why: §9 gives no sender-side reason for REJECT_UNENROLLED — a spec gap, not a builder error; `hub_not_yours` on `sent` matches §9's 'your hub does not know them'. C1 should list `not_enrolled` (and `cancelled`).

deviation_verdicts.deviation: send() during RestoreFloorRequired returns FabricError::RestorePending (contract says always 202)
deviation_verdicts.why: No epoch ⇒ no `n` can be allocated (§4 numbering is atomic with queueing); refusing is fail-closed and §4 only says existing items stay queued. The C1 'always 202' text must change and F2 must map the error (409/503 restore_pending).

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Planning MTU = current route's MTU (hub route − 120 B), else smallest registered link, else 160 B; 512 B reserve on stream links
deviation_verdicts.why: 'Destination path's profile' is the route when one exists; the smallest registered link is a sound reading of 'unknown' (a tcp-lan-only node never sends over LoRa); the reserve keeps INTRO/piggyback/wrap from overflowing.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Window fills fresh fragments first, then retransmissions, ≤ 16 outstanding
deviation_verdicts.why: §5 only bounds outstanding at 16, which holds (asserted in tests); fresh-first keeps SACK evidence flowing under no-timers.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: `node1…` pending contacts and read marks live in memory only; rebuilt from the outbox at start
deviation_verdicts.why: §7.2(2) says the node *stores* the NodeId; a contact added by NodeId with no queued message vanishes on restart (user-visible loss). Needs a small C3 table now; the read-mark half is acceptable for v1 if documented.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Startup complete_partials delivers as kind MSG (rx_frags has no kind column)
deviation_verdicts.why: v1 senders only fragment MSG; harmless until another per-stream kind fragments — keep the C3 kind-column wish on the list.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Message requests use the store's `requests` table; contacts.request unused; adding the requester's card accepts the request
deviation_verdicts.why: One source of truth, consistent reads (`request_pending`), and a scanned card is the stronger OOB act the spec contemplates.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: INTRO arriving on a non-tcp-lan link is dropped (mailbox items still accepted), provisional key zeroized
deviation_verdicts.why: Fail-closed reading of §7.2(3); a mailbox item crossed the member's tcp-lan link to its hub; test covers both the drop and the zeroize.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Stricter than §8.1: hub replies and own traffic only on attributed connections or own dials whose first announce named the peer; inbound unattributed gets nothing
deviation_verdicts.why: Strictly fail-closed; content is sealed to the pinned key either way; code path traced (`sendable_to`, `sendable_conn`, `on_sealed` gating).

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Member commits its cursor past every processed item, including one its range list deferred; hub keeps it evict-first; sender retransmits directly later; ACK via hub is fire-and-forget
deviation_verdicts.why: No fail-open: the sender keeps its copy until the recipient's ACK, the hub keeps the item until capacity; the residual (delivery waits for a direct meeting) should be written into §9 as recorded.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: The fabric never binds the tcp-lan listener; F2 calls TcpLan::listen per settings; FabricEvent::Settings for persistence
deviation_verdicts.why: Matches §8.1 ('LAN-bound when the node acts as a hub or sharing is on' is the daemon's decision); grep confirms no `listen(` call in fabric.rs.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: tcp_lan accept loop pauses 100 ms on accept() error
deviation_verdicts.why: Transport detail like keepalive (§8.1 allows timers outside the protocol); prevents an EMFILE spin.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: Events emitted before any API command runs inside a tick
deviation_verdicts.why: Preserves 'a reply never precedes the events describing its state' while keeping per-tick coalescing.

deviation_verdicts.deviation: lib.rs: only the additive `pub mod outbox;` line; stale T0 scaffold comment left in place
deviation_verdicts.why: Cosmetic; additive-only discipline respected.

result.notes:
Read first: (1) /home/kia/projects/111network/os/messaging/crates/mesh111/src/fabric.rs:569 and the `add_link` recv-forwarder (~1226-1243) against src/link/tcp_lan.rs:292 — the bounded tcp_lan channel is drained into an unbounded one, which is the OOM path (major 1); (2) `on_enroll` (fabric.rs:2539) and `on_enroll_ok` (2627) for the re-enrollment floor (major 2); (3) then the builder's own order: fabric.rs module doc, frag.rs 'SACK semantics after a receiver evicts a partial', tests/hub_flow.rs. Both majors are small, local fixes; everything else checked is sound.

What I verified by tracing: attribution happens only in `on_sealed` after `open_envelope` (pair_mac) AND `observe_counter == Fresh` (Err ⇒ Stale, fail-closed); the INTRO/tcp-lan drop precedes it; mailbox items pass `ck = None` and attribute nothing. Hub pushes: `push_to` filters `attributed == dest && push.active`; `on_fetch`/`on_custody_put`/`on_enroll` are gated on `attributed` in the dispatcher; `on_commit` streams only to attributed conns. Evicted-partial handling: receiver lists partials from `rx_snapshot`, sender applies replace semantics; convergence holds because a message is delivered in the same transaction its last bit arrives, so the sender always keeps ≥1 unSACKed fragment, and retransmit order is (id, idx)-major so lower ids complete and free slots; a stale reordered ACK can regress bits spuriously (one extra retransmit, re-ACKed as DuplicateFragment) but cannot loop. ACK selection: acked range/partial first, current newest-first, frozen [1,prefix] then ranges, ≤8, then canonical sort; the >8-ranges unit test exercises 3 epochs. tcp_lan: caps checked from the 3-byte header before `vec![0; len]`; hello then announce-first with signature + gate; back-off/keepalive/idle/handshake use tokio timers only in the adapter (allowed by §8.1); loopback refused by default; fabric never calls `listen`. Cancelled multi-fragment tombstones work (empty slices are accepted end to end). No unwrap/expect/panic in non-test F1 code; slices and casts are guarded; no wall clock in fabric/frag/outbox/mailbox/contacts.

Tests: I ran `cargo test --workspace` in a private CARGO_TARGET_DIR: 126 unit (1 ignored) + 5 + 6 + 3 integration + 2 doctests green; I did not rerun the musl checks (builder's tail shows them green). The lossy test does run 4 × 13 fragments at 160 B with 15 % loss + 15 % reorder both ways, but its `drive()` helper fires `retry_all` on 120 ms idle, so it is weaker than it looks (minor k).

Open questions for the owner / other owners: (a) should `send()` to a still-pending requester be refused (today it queues `waiting_for_key`)? harmless either way; (b) `enroll()` has no bound — F2's route must time it out, and a member whose ENROLL is judged Stale by the hub's window (restore from an older backup) hangs silently; (c) `observe_counter` is called for every verified sender including quota-refused INTRO identities — F2's CounterStore must bound per-peer window state for non-contacts or that becomes another growth path (L2/F2, not F1); (d) 'accept never ACKs more than shown' depends on C3 never pruning messages held under a pending request — worth a one-line check of the §10.4 order; (e) with the C1 contract: decide `restore_pending` on POST /messages and add `not_enrolled`/`cancelled` to the emitted set.
